**Resubmitted: deviation at the fallback level, confidence 0.79 (propose_redline ok:true, minimality passed).**

Repair to the deterministic failure ("Customer convenience termination present"):

- The earlier version only appended "for convenience, without cause" to a clause whose grammar still made the right an inference from TrueLink's wind-down duty. Following the verifier's suggested form, operation 1 now recasts Section 14 (p0079) as a **direct operative grant**: *"Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon written notice to TrueLink, and, subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month of such notice."* The wind-down date, the services description and the "subject to Section 4" qualifier are all preserved (43 words removed, 45 added).

Unchanged:

- Operation 2 still cures the material breach — TrueLink's non-renewal notice goes from thirty (30) to **ninety (90)** days, confined to the end of a term, with our own 30-day notice intact (fallback elements 3 and 4).
- Fallback element 2 remains **already_met**: no early-termination fee, penalty or unamortised charge exists anywhere; fees are charged per monthly invoice under Section 5(a).
- Preferred is expressly not claimed (no flat 30-day effective date, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees).

Flagged for a follow-up pass, outside this checklist: the stale "terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein" cross-reference (termination is Section 14), and the blank minimum support period in Section 4, which should be filled so it cannot be read to delay our convenience exit.
